requests.composed_prompt:
Generate one untouched image-model result for a controlled character-pose experiment. Treat the ordered existing-frame and skeleton pair as the exact mapping between this character and the skeleton convention. Reference inputs:

Reference 2 (subject-identity): preserve this subject's identity, proportions, design, palette, and identifying landmarks; do not copy the reference layout or pose.
Reference 3 (pose): use only its pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact; do not copy its appearance, line style, or background.
Reference 4 (pose): use only its pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact; do not copy its appearance, line style, or background.

Subject request:
Draw the same right-facing mouse in the green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, brown boots, and long tail in the target running pose. Keep the character design identical to the matched existing frame while changing the complete body pose to follow the target skeleton. Use a plain white background.

The four reference images are ordered: (1) approved character identity, (2) an existing frame of that character, (3) the skeleton matched to image 2, and (4) the target skeleton. Images 2 and 3 define how this skeleton maps to the character. Draw the character from image 2 in image 4's pose.
Animation frame 4 of 12. Render exactly one fresh right-facing character image. Do not return a sheet, turnaround, wireframe, skeleton, or edited reference board.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one square pixel-art animation frame, frame 4 of 12
Primary request: Generate exactly one fresh image of the same right-facing mouse character from Images 1 and 2, redrawn in the complete target running pose from Image 4.
Input images:
- Image 1: approved subject-identity reference. Preserve the mouse identity, proportions, character design, palette, identifying landmarks, costume, pixel-art line quality, viewing direction, and character scale. Do not copy its pose or layout.
- Image 2: existing approved animation frame and subject-identity reference. Preserve this exact character. Together with Image 3, it defines the exact mapping between the character anatomy/costume and the skeleton convention. Do not copy Image 2's pose.
- Image 3: pose skeleton matched to Image 2. Use only to understand how every skeleton joint and segment maps to this mouse's pelvis, spine, head, arms, legs, and feet. Do not render this skeleton and do not copy its pose.
- Image 4: sole target pose. Follow its right-facing running pose exactly for pelvis position, torso/spine lean, head location and facing, both shoulders/arms/hands, both hips/legs/knees, both feet, and ground contact.
Scene/backdrop: plain solid white background only.
Subject: one small anthropomorphic mouse facing right, with tan-brown fur, very large rounded pink inner ears, pointed muzzle, long thin tail, green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt with small buckle, brown boots; identical design to Images 1 and 2.
Style/medium: crisp low-resolution hand-pixeled game sprite aesthetic matching Images 1 and 2 exactly; preserve their palette, clustered pixel shading, dark pixel outlines, proportions, detail density, and scale.
Composition/framing: 1:1 square canvas; one complete character; no cropping; place the character according to the target skeleton and its ground line while keeping the sprite scale consistent with Images 1 and 2.
Pose fidelity: Treat the ordered Image 2 + Image 3 pair as the exact anatomical mapping, then transfer the character unchanged onto Image 4's pose. This is a controlled pose experiment. The target skeleton overrides the example-frame pose. Represent all four limbs distinctly and completely, including both arms, both hands/paws, both legs, and both boots/feet, with their bends and overlaps matching Image 4.
Constraints: Output exactly one PNG image and one animation frame only. Preserve identity, proportions, costume, colors, line quality, right-facing view, and scale. Change the complete body pose to Image 4. Keep the long tail.
Avoid: do not copy the example pose; do not omit, merge, duplicate, or invent limbs; no skeleton lines, joint markers, guides, labels, text, sprite sheet, turnaround, wireframe, reference board, scenery, cast shadows, extra characters, watermark, border, or transparent/checkerboard background.
